name: DEC Advisory Reports
summary: Practical energy recommendations to accompany a Display Energy Certificate.
intro: A Display Energy Certificate shows how a qualifying public building uses energy. Its advisory report supports that rating with recommendations. Request a review for an existing Birmingham or the West Midlands building where the report is missing, needs renewing or no longer reflects the operational context.
focus: Operational energy and a practical improvement plan
cases: Publicly occupied buildings reviewing their DEC documentation
Facilities teams gathering an energy improvement programme
Building managers checking an inherited advisory report

sections.title: A companion to the operational rating
sections.text: The advisory report is a separate document from the DEC itself. It identifies opportunities to improve energy performance; it does not record completed upgrades or guarantee a reduction in bills. If you need both documents, include that in the enquiry so the scope can be agreed together.

sections.title: Start with the building and its actual operation
sections.text: Supply the address, floor area, building use, available energy records and any existing DEC or advisory report. Explain changes in occupancy, opening hours or the areas included. The information needed for the certificate and report should be confirmed before work is arranged.

sections.title: Turn the recommendations into decisions
sections.text: An advisory report can help organise further investigation and improvement work. Costs, technical feasibility and building constraints still need consideration before a recommendation becomes a project. A later EPC or a building-services design is a separate instruction.

faqs.question: Is this the same as a DEC?
faqs.answer: No. The DEC is the operational energy rating; the advisory report provides associated recommendations. We can review an enquiry for either or both.

faqs.question: Do all commercial properties need one?
faqs.answer: No. DEC requirements concern qualifying public buildings. Private commercial premises should not be assumed to need a DEC simply because members of the public visit.

faqs.question: Can an old report be reused?
faqs.answer: Send the existing report and details of the current building. Its applicability and validity need checking rather than assuming it still covers the instruction.

name: MEES Compliance Assessments
summary: Review EPC ratings, letting circumstances and improvement evidence for MEES.
intro: If you let an existing commercial property, the EPC rating is only part of the MEES picture. A Birmingham or the West Midlands assessment enquiry should also identify the tenancy, any relevant exclusions or exemptions and the evidence already held by the landlord.
focus: Understand the letting position before committing to works
cases: Landlords preparing an existing unit for a new letting
Managing agents reviewing an EPC F or G property
Owners gathering evidence for improvement or exemption review

sections.title: Review the rule that applies to the property
sections.text: The current minimum standard for in-scope non-domestic rented property is EPC E, subject to the regulations and applicable exemptions. A review needs to consider whether the premises and tenancy fall within scope. Future policy proposals should not be treated as a rule already applying to the building.

sections.title: Separate improvements from exemptions
sections.text: Provide the existing EPC, recommendation report, lease information and any registered exemption records. A poor rating does not automatically mean an exemption is available. Equally, an EPC alone does not establish the full legal position for a particular letting.

sections.title: A documented route to the next decision
sections.text: The review can identify evidence gaps, rating improvement options and matters requiring specialist advice. An EPC reassessment, installation work or legal opinion may be separate from the initial assessment. No target rating or lawful letting outcome is guaranteed in advance.

faqs.question: Does MEES apply to every building?
faqs.answer: No. The non-domestic rented-property rules have a defined scope. Provide the property and letting details so applicability can be reviewed.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee an EPC E rating?
faqs.answer: No. The rating depends on the building, services and supported assessment inputs. Any improvement scenario needs checking against the actual property.

faqs.question: Is an exemption automatic if works are expensive?
faqs.answer: No. Exemptions have criteria and evidence requirements. The appropriate basis and registration position need review.

name: EPC Improvement Reports
summary: Assess practical options to improve an existing commercial EPC rating.
intro: Before spending money on an existing building, understand which changes may influence its EPC. An improvement-report enquiry for Birmingham or the West Midlands brings together the current certificate, available evidence and proposed works so the options can be considered in context.
focus: Explore the rating options before commissioning upgrades
cases: Landlords considering upgrades before remarketing
Owners reviewing a low commercial EPC rating
Agents comparing proposed lighting, heating or fabric changes

sections.title: Check the starting point
sections.text: Supply the current EPC and recommendation report, plans and evidence of the installed services. Changes made since the assessment may need documenting. An improvement exercise is more useful when the existing building information is accurate and the intended outcome is clear.

sections.title: Compare measures as a building-specific package
sections.text: Lighting, controls, heating, cooling and fabric measures can affect the assessment differently. A report should explain which options warrant further examination and what evidence supports the assumptions. A generic shopping list is not a prediction of the resulting EPC band.

sections.title: Keep the final certificate separate
sections.text: A prospective improvement report is not a replacement EPC and does not itself change the public rating. Completed works, supporting evidence and any subsequent assessment need to be dealt with before a new certificate can be issued. Installation specifications and costs require their own review.

faqs.question: Will the report change the registered rating?
faqs.answer: No. It supports decisions about improvements. A new certificate requires the appropriate assessment and lodgement.

faqs.question: Can proposed works be compared?
faqs.answer: Yes, describe the options and provide specifications where available. The quotation should define what comparison or modelling is included.

faqs.question: Are energy savings guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. An EPC rating and actual consumption are different measures. Occupancy, operation and weather also affect bills.

name: Commercial Energy Audits
summary: Investigate building energy use and practical efficiency opportunities.
intro: For an existing office, retail unit, warehouse or mixed commercial site, an energy audit starts with how energy is actually being used. Share your Birmingham or the West Midlands building details and the decisions you want the audit to support.
focus: Find out where energy is going
cases: Facilities teams investigating rising consumption
Businesses comparing operating hours with control schedules
Owners prioritising efficiency work across existing premises

sections.title: Set a useful boundary
sections.text: Define whether the enquiry covers one building, a tenant area or several sites. Include available bills, meter data, hours of use and information about major equipment. State any known changes that make one period difficult to compare with another.

sections.title: Look at operation alongside equipment
sections.text: An audit can investigate operating patterns, controls, heating and cooling interaction, lighting and other significant loads. The agreed scope determines the level of site investigation and analysis. Missing meter or asset information should be identified at the start.

sections.title: Prioritise actions with clear assumptions
sections.text: The findings can separate operational changes from measures requiring investment or further investigation. Any estimate depends on the evidence, tariffs and assumptions used. An audit does not replace a commercial EPC, statutory air-conditioning inspection or an ESOS assessment where one is required.

faqs.question: Is this the same as an EPC?
faqs.answer: No. An EPC is a standardised building rating. An audit focuses on energy use and improvement opportunities within the agreed scope.

faqs.question: Do I need interval meter data?
faqs.answer: It can help, but send what you have. The available data and any limitations should inform the quotation.

faqs.question: Does an audit automatically satisfy ESOS?
faqs.answer: No. ESOS has organisation-level requirements and a specific compliance process. Tell us if that is the purpose of the enquiry.

name: ESOS Compliance Assessments
summary: Scope organisation-level ESOS assessment and evidence requirements.
intro: ESOS is an organisation-level energy assessment scheme, not a certificate required for every individual commercial building. For an organisation with existing premises in Birmingham or the West Midlands, start by describing the entity, group structure and energy activities included.
cases: Organisations reviewing ESOS qualification
Groups coordinating evidence from existing commercial sites
Energy managers planning assessment and reporting work

sections.title: Establish whether the organisation qualifies
sections.text: Qualification is assessed against the scheme rules and relevant phase. A building’s size or EPC rating alone does not answer the question. Supply group and organisational information so the relevant participation and assessment requirements can be reviewed.

sections.title: Agree the energy and evidence scope
sections.text: ESOS can cover buildings, transport and industrial processes. Even if your initial enquiry concerns an existing building, describe the wider operations and any assessment evidence already available. A site-only audit should not be represented as complete organisation-wide compliance.

sections.title: Confirm responsibilities and deliverables
sections.text: The quotation should identify the assessment work, any lead-assessor involvement, evidence preparation and reporting support included. Current phase requirements, action planning and notification responsibilities need checking for the organisation. The initial enquiry does not confirm qualification, assessor availability or a compliant outcome.

faqs.question: Is every commercial landlord in ESOS?
faqs.answer: No. The scheme applies to qualifying organisations under its own rules. An individual property does not automatically create a requirement.

faqs.question: Can existing energy audits help?
faqs.answer: Potentially. Their coverage, quality and dates need review against the relevant scheme requirements.

faqs.question: Will a building inspection complete the whole process?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. Organisational scope, evidence, assessment and reporting requirements must be considered together.

intro: If your Birmingham or the West Midlands building has refrigerant-based equipment, provide the refrigerant type, charge information and system records before arranging a leak check. Requirements depend on the equipment and applicable rules rather than a single timetable for every air-conditioning unit.
focus: Refrigerant information and equipment records first
cases: Building managers checking equipment records
Operators reviewing leak-check requirements after changes
Facilities teams distinguishing TM44 from refrigerant duties

sections.title: Identify the installation
sections.text: Send the make, model, refrigerant designation, charge information and any existing logbook. Label photographs can help locate the relevant information. Include details of leak-detection equipment if present rather than assuming a standard arrangement.

sections.title: Confirm the appropriate check
sections.text: The applicable requirements depend on the gas, equipment and charge information. Work involving regulated refrigerants must be undertaken by personnel with the relevant qualifications and, where required, an appropriately certified business. The correct provider and scope need confirmation before the work is booked.

sections.title: Keep repairs and inspection duties distinct
sections.text: A leak-check enquiry is not an instruction to replace refrigerant, repair equipment or certify every aspect of the installation. Describe any known leak or recent repair so the required work and follow-up can be established. Routine servicing and TM44 energy inspections are separate matters.

faqs.question: Is a TM44 report enough?
faqs.answer: No. TM44 concerns energy efficiency. Refrigerant leak checks have a different purpose and regulatory basis.

faqs.question: Is there one inspection interval for all units?
faqs.answer: No. The relevant requirements depend on the equipment and refrigerant information. Send the records for review.

faqs.question: Can repairs be included?
faqs.answer: Describe the known problem. Repairs, any refrigerant work and follow-up requirements must be specifically agreed.

name: TR19 Ventilation Hygiene Inspections
summary: Review ventilation cleanliness, access and hygiene evidence in existing buildings.
intro: For a Birmingham or the West Midlands commercial ventilation system, an inspection enquiry should identify what the ductwork serves and why it is being reviewed. General ventilation hygiene and kitchen-extract grease management require different considerations.
focus: Know the system before choosing the inspection scope
cases: Facilities teams reviewing general ventilation cleanliness
Managers checking duct access and cleaning records
Operators distinguishing kitchen extract from general ventilation

sections.title: Distinguish air systems from grease extract
sections.text: TR19 Air concerns ventilation-system hygiene. Kitchen extraction with grease contamination is addressed through a different TR19 Grease context. State which systems are involved; do not assume a general ventilation inspection is a kitchen fire-risk assessment.

sections.title: Map the system and its access
sections.text: Provide duct drawings where available, the rooms served, access-panel information, previous inspection or cleaning reports and any concerns about contamination. An inspection of accessible areas cannot establish the condition of concealed sections that have not been examined.

sections.title: Agree evidence and follow-up work
sections.text: Confirm the inspection method, areas included and form of reporting in the quotation. Cleaning, access alterations, remedial work and post-clean verification should be identified separately where needed. The use of a technical standard does not establish that a business holds a particular certification.

faqs.question: Is this automatically a duct-cleaning service?
faqs.answer: No. Inspection, cleaning and verification are distinct activities. Tell us which outcomes you need so the scope can be agreed.

faqs.question: Does it cover kitchen extraction?
faqs.answer: Mention kitchen extraction explicitly. Grease-extract risks need the appropriate scope and should not be treated as ordinary ventilation hygiene.

faqs.question: Can a report cover inaccessible ductwork?
faqs.answer: Access limitations need recording. Additional access or investigation may be required before conclusions can be drawn about concealed sections.

name: Asbestos Management Surveys
summary: Assess accessible suspect materials to support management of existing premises.
intro: An asbestos management survey helps a dutyholder understand materials that may be encountered during normal occupation and foreseeable maintenance. Request a scope for an existing Birmingham or the West Midlands commercial building, with the register and access information you already hold.
focus: Manage the occupied building with a clear record
cases: Dutyholders reviewing an existing asbestos register
Managing agents taking on older commercial premises
Owners identifying gaps in normal-occupation survey records

sections.title: Understand what a management survey covers
sections.text: Its purpose is to locate, as far as reasonably practicable, suspect asbestos-containing materials that could be disturbed during normal occupation, routine maintenance or installation of equipment. The planned access, sampling approach and limitations should be discussed before the survey.

sections.title: Keep intrusive works separate
sections.text: A management survey is not a substitute for a refurbishment or demolition survey before intrusive work. If an alteration or demolition is planned, describe it before accepting a management-survey quotation. This page concerns management of existing commercial premises, not a new-build service.

sections.title: Use the survey within a management process
sections.text: The survey information supports the asbestos register and management plan; a survey alone does not discharge every duty. Provide earlier reports, plans, areas of restricted access and the site contact. Known suspect materials should not be disturbed to prepare for the visit.

faqs.question: Does a management survey prove there is no asbestos?
faqs.answer: No. Access and survey limitations matter, and some materials may be presumed to contain asbestos. Read the report and limitations with the register.

faqs.question: Will sampling always be included?
faqs.answer: The sampling approach must be agreed for the property. Access, occupancy and material condition can affect the work.

faqs.question: Can it be used before refurbishment?
faqs.answer: It should not be assumed sufficient. The planned work may require a different, more intrusive survey scope.

intro: A water-hygiene enquiry for existing Birmingham or the West Midlands premises can bring together the system layout, operating records and concerns about water quality or use. The assessment should address a defined system and purpose rather than promise a universal water-safety certificate.

cases: Facilities teams reviewing tanks, outlets and records
Managers reopening underused parts of an existing building
Owners checking water-hygiene arrangements after a change of occupation

sections.title: Define the system being reviewed
sections.text: Identify the water supply, storage, hot-water arrangements and outlets included. State whether the enquiry concerns drinking water, domestic hot and cold water or a specialist system. Different systems require different expertise and assessment methods.

sections.title: Review records as well as visible condition
sections.text: Provide previous risk assessments, schematic information, maintenance records and available monitoring results. Describe periods of low use, changes in occupation and any reported concern. The inspection scope should make clear what can be checked and what needs further investigation.

sections.title: Use targeted testing where it is justified
sections.text: Sampling is not automatically required for every system or every enquiry. Any testing should have a defined purpose, method and interpretation. A broader hygiene review should not be represented as a replacement for a suitable Legionella risk assessment where one is needed.

faqs.question: Is this the same as a Legionella risk assessment?
faqs.answer: No. The scope can overlap, but a general condition-and-records review should not be treated as a Legionella risk assessment unless that work is expressly included.

faqs.question: Will every outlet be sampled?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. The purpose and extent of any sampling should be agreed based on the system and concerns.

faqs.question: Can a vacant building be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Yes, explain the period of low use and planned reopening. The scope and any precautions need to reflect the actual circumstances.

name: Commercial Electrical EICR Inspections
summary: Inspect and test the condition of an existing commercial electrical installation.
intro: An Electrical Installation Condition Report records findings from inspection and testing of the fixed installation within an agreed scope. For Birmingham or the West Midlands premises, provide the earlier report, distribution-board information and operating constraints before arranging the work.
focus: An installation-specific scope with planned access
cases: Businesses reviewing an inherited fixed-wiring report
Landlords agreeing an inspection scope with occupiers
Facilities managers planning testing around trading hours

sections.title: Define the fixed installation and limitations
sections.text: Identify the buildings, areas, distribution boards and circuits included. Supply plans, earlier reports and records of alterations where available. Restricted access and agreed limitations should be recorded rather than assuming every circuit can be fully examined during normal trading.

sections.title: Plan isolation and business continuity
sections.text: Inspection and testing can require isolation or interruption to circuits. Explain critical equipment, alarms, IT loads, occupied areas and any out-of-hours requirement before a quotation is agreed. The work should be undertaken by a person competent for the installation and testing involved.

sections.title: Separate findings from remedial work
sections.text: An EICR reports the condition found within its scope and uses classification codes for observations. Repairs, further investigation and subsequent confirmation of work should be specifically agreed. There is no single inspection interval that can safely be assumed for every commercial property.

faqs.question: Does an EICR include portable appliance testing?
faqs.answer: Not as a default. An EICR concerns the fixed installation; appliance inspection or testing is a separate scope.

faqs.question: Will there be a power interruption?
faqs.answer: Testing may need isolation. Tell us about critical operations so the access and outage plan can be discussed.

faqs.question: Are repairs automatically included?
faqs.answer: No. Remedial work and any further investigation should be separately defined in the quotation.

name: Emergency Lighting Inspections
summary: Review emergency-lighting condition, testing evidence and identified defects.
intro: For an existing Birmingham or the West Midlands workplace, emergency-lighting inspection should be scoped around the actual escape routes, system and available records. Share the fire risk assessment, logbook and any known faults so the required checks can be discussed.
focus: Escape routes, test records and operational planning
cases: Responsible persons reviewing gaps in lighting records
Managers investigating failed or damaged luminaires
Occupiers coordinating testing with a shared-building landlord

sections.title: Start with the system and the fire-safety context
sections.text: Identify maintained or non-maintained equipment where known, the areas served and the person managing the testing. The fire risk assessment can help explain the role of emergency lighting in the premises. An inspection does not itself establish a complete fire-safety strategy.

sections.title: Agree the inspection and testing method
sections.text: Routine functional checks, duration testing and a review of design or coverage are not interchangeable. Specify which is needed and provide existing drawings and records. Testing must be planned so occupied escape routes are not left without appropriate protection while equipment recovers.

sections.title: Record findings and agree corrective work
sections.text: The report should identify the scope, findings and relevant limitations. Battery replacements, repairs, additional luminaires and design changes should be agreed separately. Frequencies and procedures must follow the system, risk assessment and applicable guidance rather than an invented universal timetable.

faqs.question: Is this included in a fire risk assessment?
faqs.answer: A fire risk assessment may review arrangements, but it does not automatically include electrical testing of emergency lighting. Define both requirements.

faqs.question: Can testing take place during occupation?
faqs.answer: The visit needs planning around the system and premises. Explain opening hours and any areas that cannot be taken out of use.

faqs.question: Does a test prove the lighting design is adequate?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Functional testing and verification of coverage or design are different scopes.

name: Commercial Gas Safety Inspections
summary: Scope gas-safety inspection work for existing commercial appliances and systems.
intro: Commercial gas installations vary from office heating to catering equipment and specialist appliances. For a Birmingham or the West Midlands enquiry, identify the appliances, gas type and intended inspection so the work can be matched to an engineer with the appropriate competence and registration categories.
focus: The right appliance information and engineer category
cases: Workplace managers reviewing gas maintenance records
Operators arranging inspection of commercial catering equipment
Owners taking over existing gas-fired plant

sections.title: Identify the installation and intended evidence
sections.text: Send the address, appliance types, available model details and previous records. Explain whether the premises include commercial kitchens, plant rooms or shared systems. Different appliances and gas types can require different engineer categories and inspection scopes.

sections.title: Confirm competence for the work
sections.text: Gas work within the applicable registration requirements must be undertaken by a Gas Safe registered engineer qualified for the specific work. Registration alone should not be taken to cover every commercial appliance. The suitable provider and availability must be confirmed before the instruction.

sections.title: Keep inspection, servicing and repairs clear
sections.text: An inspection does not automatically include servicing, repair work or assessment of every connected system. Applicable workplace duties and any landlord responsibilities should be considered for the circumstances. Do not assume a domestic landlord timetable or a generic certificate covers every commercial installation.

faqs.question: Is there one commercial gas certificate for every site?
faqs.answer: No single description establishes the scope. Identify the appliances, premises and evidence required so the correct work can be agreed.

faqs.question: Does the inspection include servicing?
faqs.answer: Only if specified. Inspection, servicing and remedial work should be clear in the quotation.

faqs.question: What if the engineer finds a safety concern?
faqs.answer: The engineer must follow the applicable safety procedures for the circumstances. Known concerns should be reported when arranging the work; urgent situations need the appropriate emergency response.

sections.text: DEC duties depend on the building meeting the relevant public-authority occupation, public-access and floor-area conditions. Note shared supplies, separate occupiers and significant changes in use. The assessor will need to establish which energy use and area belong to the instruction.

sections.title: Keep the certificate and advice connected
sections.text: The DEC and its associated advisory report are distinct documents with related purposes. Tell us whether you need both. The report can inform an improvement programme, but it is not a detailed design or a guarantee of savings. Any additional audit, EPC or technical investigation should be separately agreed.

faqs.question: Is a DEC the same as a commercial EPC?
faqs.answer: No. A DEC describes operational energy performance for a qualifying building; a commercial EPC is a standardised asset rating.

faqs.question: Can shared meters make the assessment more complex?

intro: For Birmingham offices, retail premises and other existing commercial buildings, a TM44 enquiry starts with the installed cooling systems. Share the cooling capacities, served rooms and previous inspection records so the appropriate scope can be discussed.

cases: Facilities teams checking previous air-conditioning reports

Building operators coordinating plant access across occupations

sections.title: Review capacity and technical control
sections.text: The inspection requirement concerns systems with an effective rated output above 12kW. Several individual units under common technical control may count together. The relevant cooling output should come from equipment records rather than an estimate based on building size.

sections.title: Know what the inspection is for
sections.text: A TM44 inspection considers energy efficiency, controls, sizing and operation. It is separate from refrigerant leak checks, routine servicing and a commercial EPC. Describe specialist or process-related equipment separately so its purpose can be considered in the scoping discussion.

sections.title: Prepare for an accredited assessment
sections.text: Qualifying systems require inspection at intervals no more than five years apart. A valid statutory report must be produced and lodged by an accredited air-conditioning energy assessor. Provide the equipment schedule, previous report, operating hours and access arrangements before availability and price are agreed.

faqs.question: Do several small units count together?
faqs.answer: They can where they are under common technical control. Send the complete equipment schedule for review.

faqs.question: Does an F-Gas check replace TM44?
faqs.answer: No. Refrigerant checks and an air-conditioning energy inspection have different purposes.

faqs.question: Will repairs or control adjustments be included?

Operators responding to changes in use or layout

sections.text: Identify the floors or units included, the occupiers and the person coordinating fire-safety arrangements. Shared routes or systems may require cooperation between responsible persons. A single postal address does not necessarily establish one complete assessment boundary.

sections.title: Provide evidence of the current arrangements
sections.text: Send the previous assessment, available plans and records for relevant fire precautions. Explain changes in layout, staffing, storage or occupation and identify known concerns. Access is needed to understand the agreed areas; restrictions should be recorded rather than overlooked.

sections.title: Use the findings as part of ongoing management
sections.text: The assessment should identify hazards, evaluate risk and support appropriate actions. It is not a blanket compliance certificate, nor does it automatically include testing of alarms, emergency lighting or electrical installations. The responsible person must manage the findings and keep the assessment under review as circumstances require.

faqs.question: Does an assessment include alarm or lighting tests?
faqs.answer: Not by default. A review of arrangements and specialist testing are different scopes.

faqs.question: Can a multi-occupied property be assessed?
faqs.answer: Describe the occupations, common areas and responsible persons so the boundaries and cooperation requirements can be agreed.

faqs.question: Is one visit a guarantee of compliance?

intro: For existing Birmingham commercial premises, a Legionella risk assessment should reflect the water systems and the people potentially exposed. Share the system information, occupancy patterns and previous control records rather than assuming every building needs the same checks.
focus: Know the water system. Understand the risk.
cases: Managers taking responsibility for existing hot and cold water systems
Operators reopening areas after low use
Dutyholders reviewing changes in occupancy or water-system use

sections.title: Identify the systems and use patterns
sections.text: Provide information on storage, hot-water generation, showers and other relevant outlets or equipment. Explain low-use areas, vulnerable occupants where relevant to the assessment and any recent changes. A plan or schematic helps establish the extent of the review.

sections.title: Review evidence and management responsibilities
sections.text: Include previous risk assessments, monitoring records, maintenance information and the person responsible for managing the system. The assessment needs to consider risk and existing controls together. Missing records should be flagged so the quotation reflects the available evidence.

sections.title: Agree proportionate follow-up
sections.text: The findings can inform a control scheme, further investigation or changes to management arrangements. faqs.question: Is water sampling always part of the assessment?
faqs.answer: No. Sampling needs a defined purpose and may not be necessary for every system. The proposed approach should follow the assessed circumstances.

faqs.question: Is a water-hygiene inspection the same service?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. A broader condition or records review does not replace a Legionella risk assessment unless that scope is expressly included.

faqs.question: What if parts of the building have been unused?
faqs.answer: Explain the period of low use and planned reopening so stagnation and management arrangements can be considered.
